name: Alert dialog
description: A Dialog that interrupts the user to confirm or acknowledge something important, such as deleting a file. It stays open until the user picks a response.
summary: Interrupts to confirm a consequential action

elements.name: Title
elements.description: States the question or warning; referenced by aria-labelledby

elements.name: Message
elements.description: Explains the consequence; referenced by aria-describedby

elements.name: Confirm button
elements.description: Names the action, such as "Delete file"

elements.name: Cancel button
elements.description: Closes without acting; left out only when the dialog just needs acknowledging

elements.name: Backdrop
elements.description: Covers the page; the dialog is always modal

configOptions.options: None, Leading icon beside the title

variants.caption: Icon — warning icon beside the title

usageNotes: Use an Alert dialog only when the user must respond before going on, such as confirming a deletion. For information that needs no decision, use an Alert or a Toast.
Open it with showModal() and set role="alertdialog", with aria-labelledby pointing at the title and aria-describedby at the message, so screen readers announce both.
Move focus into the dialog when it opens. The APG suggests focusing the least destructive action, usually Cancel, when the confirm action can't be undone.
Label buttons with the action ("Delete", "Keep editing") rather than "Yes" and "No", so the choice makes sense without rereading the message.
Escape should close it as Cancel, and focus should return to the control that opened it.
htmlOutline:
Delete file?

This can't be undone.
